text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are strong — but who do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD.
Yet he too is wise, and he brings disaster; he does not take back his words. He will rise against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who do wrong.
The Egyptians are only human, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the one helped will fall, and both will perish together.

For this is what the LORD has said to me: As a lion, a young lion, growls over its prey — and though a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not frightened by their shouting or dismayed by their uproar — so the LORD of hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.

versions.text: For this is what the LORD has said to me: As a lion growls, a young lion over its prey — and though a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not frightened by their shouting or dismayed by their uproar — so the LORD of hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
versions.explanation: The clipped phrase "As a lion growls, a young lion over its prey" stumbles when read aloud; recasting keeps both nouns with a single verb, as in the Hebrew. Also, גִּבְעָתָהּ is singular ("its hill"), matching the paired singular "Mount Zion."

text: Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem; he will shield and deliver it, he will pass over it and rescue it.
Return, people of Israel, to the one against whom you have so deeply rebelled.
For on that day everyone will reject his own idols of silver and idols of gold, which your hands have made for you as a sin.

versions.text: For on that day everyone will reject the idols of silver and the idols of gold that your own sinful hands have made.
versions.explanation: Two nuances are lost: the Hebrew has the possessive ("his silver idols and his gold idols"), stressing personal ownership of the idols; and חֵטְא describes the idols themselves as "a sin," not the hands as "sinful." The revision restores both without harming the flow.

text: Then Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; a sword not wielded by mortals will devour them. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
Their stronghold will pass away in terror, and their officers will be shattered at the sight of the battle standard, declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
